land.text: Maimana, which the Ming family had governed since 1621; independent with the death of Nader Shah in 1747

rulers.name: Hajji Bi Khan Ming
rulers.note: The first independent ruler; the page lists the rulers after Jonathan Lee. The list's reign start is 1731; clipped to the khanate's founding in 1747 (reviewer, ia-03-x).

rulers.name: Hukumat Khan
rulers.note: Shared rule with Sher Muhammad Khan 1845-1848.

ledger.note: 1747: Maimana becomes independent. 'It was founded in 1747 with the death of Nader Shah'; the Ming family had governed it since 1621 and Hajji Bi Ming was its first independent ruler.
1814: Sar-i Pul secedes. 'After the death of Ahmad Khan in 1814, Sar-i Pul seceded from the khanate'; in the 1830s Sar-i Pul took Gurziwan.
1845: the Aimaq of the Murghab break away. 'The Aimaq tribes of the Murghab broke away by 1845.' The land is not placed on the page; the year is the page's bound.

region.text: the khanate: Maimana and its districts (Almar, Andkhoy etc.); the page gives no frontier

ledger.note: 1876: Afghanistan annexes Maimana. After the khanate 'rebelled against Afghanistan but it was crushed and the city sacked' (1875), 'From March 1876 to February 1879, the khanate was annexed into Afghanistan, and Afghan governors were appointed.'

region.text: the khanate: Maimana and its districts (Almar, Andkhoy etc.); the page gives no frontier

ledger.note: 1879: the khanate is restored. Afghan governors end in February 1879 on the page; the next ruler listed, Dilawar Khan, dates from February 1880.

region.text: the khanate: Maimana and its districts (Almar, Andkhoy etc.); the page gives no frontier

ledger.note: 1892: Afghanistan annexes the Maimana Khanate. 'In 1892 the khanate was annexed by Afghanistan.'

wars.name: Herat attempts to annex Maimana
wars.outcome: Maimana resisted: Yar Mohammad Khan of Herat marched in 1847 and retreated in early 1848; a siege from November 1849 was lifted in September 1850.
wars.note: 'In 1847 and 1850 it resisted attempts by the Emirate of Herat to annex it.'

wars.name: Afghan annexation of Maimana
wars.outcome: The 1875 rebellion was crushed and the city sacked; Maimana was annexed from March 1876 to February 1879 and again in 1892.

certainty.note: No frontier is described on the page; the oasis and steppe edges with Herat, Andkhoy, Sar-i Pul and Murghab are approximate.

sources.title: Maimana Khanate
sources.note: Founded 1747, rulers (Jonathan Lee), Sar-i Pul secedes after 1814, Aimaq of the Murghab break away by 1845, resists Herat 1847 and 1850, annexed March 1876-February 1879, annexed 1892.

notes: Written for batch ia-03-x from one page (MM; budget 3-5). The page gives no area, no frontier and no dated vassalage to the Durranis, Persia, Bukhara or Afghanistan (it only notes Bukhara's role in the 1845 Chahar Wilayat conflict), so no vassal pair is recorded; ia-03-e's durrani-empire dossier records a vassal_end of 1823 for Maimana, which this page neither supports nor contradicts. The 1879/2 restoration is confidence 2: the rulers list resumes in February 1880. Counterparts Sar-i Pul (a seceding chiefdom) and the Murghab Aimaq (nobody) have no dossier. The shape is Faryab (and Sari Pul to 1813) as a floor.
